data.title: Ozenoxacin 1% cream
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Non-fluorinated quinolone (topical only)

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits both bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV → bactericidal
- Dual-target binding means a lower chance of resistance; active against MRSA and quinolone-resistant strains, and Streptococcus pyogenes

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Impetigo (non-bullous and bullous, localised) in adults and children 2 months and older

## Dose & formulations
- Thin layer twice daily for 5 days (up to 100 cm² in adults; 2% BSA in children)

## Adverse effects
- Rare: application-site itching, rosacea flare, seborrhoeic dermatitis

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; not for eyes, mouth or mucosa

## Pregnancy & lactation
Negligible absorption — acceptable.

## Viva points
- Newer impetigo treatment; works against MRSA and mupirocin-resistant staph
- 5-day course, twice daily

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41 (Topical antibacterial agents — ozenoxacin). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
